meta.title: AI Workflow Automation Documents
meta.description: DDD documentation framework for AI Workflow / Agent automation projects (Make.com, n8n, Pabbly, Claude Agent SDK, multi-agent harness). AI reads this file and generates .md files in the correct order with proper cross-references.
meta.applicable_when: Building scheduled or event-driven AI workflows that orchestrate LLM calls, MCP tool calls, and external integrations to produce a recurring deliverable (briefs, reports, classifications, automations) — distinct from web/mobile applications. Distinct from the context-formalization template, whose assembled bundle is the runtime context this harness feeds to a model rather than something this template produces, and from the optimization-theory template, which tunes the parameters this template declares (budgets, thresholds, retrieval settings) rather than defining the workflow itself.

agent_instructions.role: You are an AI workflow documentation generator. Read this file and produce each document listed in phases[], in dependency order.
agent_instructions.generation_order_strategy: Topological sort by depends_on graph. Generate documents with no dependencies first. Each document is the canonical source for its concerns — downstream docs reference upstream docs by document ID. Enum values are defined once in their owner document and only indexed in GLOSSARY.md's Enumeration Registry — downstream documents reference an enum by name, never redefine its values.
agent_instructions.content_language: Write document content in Thai for narrative sections; use English for all identifiers, code, prompt template names, model names, MCP tool names, and technical terms. Preserve jargon (LLM, MCP, agent, harness, prompt, evaluator) as English even in Thai sentences.
agent_instructions.quality_gate: Each document must cover all sections[] listed. Validate that cross-references (refs[]) resolve to real document IDs before finishing. Every harness component, every prompt template, every MCP tool used must be documented exactly once in its canonical doc and referenced elsewhere — no duplicate definitions. Never hardcode the adopting organization's own name, its customers, or its domains — use placeholders so the template stays reusable; naming the third-party platforms and vendor tools the workflow actually integrates with is expected, since those are part of the domain being documented. Every enum is defined in exactly one owner document and only indexed in GLOSSARY.md's Enumeration Registry — other documents reference it, never redefine it. Never invent a default for a value that needs calibration (retry count, backoff window, circuit-breaker threshold, timeout, token or cost budget, eval threshold, retention period) — declare it null with its calibration source and owner instead.
domain_specific_notes: AI Workflow ≠ Web App. There is no UI, no users in real-time. The 'output' is a generated artifact (brief, report, action) delivered through a channel.
The 'architecture' equivalent is HARNESS.md — describing the orchestration scaffold around the LLM(s).
The 'API spec' equivalent is INTEGRATION_SPEC.md — describing inbound triggers + outbound delivery channels + MCP tool calls.
The 'data model' equivalent is DATA_CONTRACTS.md — describing JSON schemas at each stage boundary, structured outputs from LLMs, and persistent state (memory store).
The 'testing' equivalent is EVALUATION.md — describing how to grade LLM output quality (citation grounding, hallucination check, format compliance, end-user usefulness).
PROMPT_SPEC.md is unique to AI workflows — every system/user prompt template is versioned and lives here as the single source of truth.
Cost is a first-class concern (per-run cost, per-month cost, per-token economics) — must be tracked in DEPLOYMENT_OPS.md.

Stage boundary ≠ agent boundary ≠ subagent boundary — DATA_CONTRACTS.md schemas govern stage boundaries; the agent-to-agent handoff payload and the subagent return contract are separate contracts (HARNESS.md agent topology and CONTEXT_PLAN.md subagent isolation respectively). Reusing one schema for all three hides who is allowed to see what.

Retry ≠ replay ≠ resume — retry re-attempts one failed call inside a live run (HARNESS.md control flow); replay re-executes a finished run from its recorded inputs to reproduce or audit it; resume continues a partially-completed run from its last checkpoint without redoing committed side effects. Each needs different state and different idempotency guarantees.

Cross-run memory ≠ intra-run state ≠ context window — the memory store (DATA_CONTRACTS.md) persists across runs, intra-run execution state records which stages already completed within one run, and the context window is what the model actually sees on a given call (CONTEXT_PLAN.md budget). Conflating them produces a workflow that cannot resume and a context that silently overflows.

Prompt version ≠ model version ≠ harness config version — PROMPT_SPEC.md versions the template text, MODEL_LIFECYCLE.md versions which model ID is pinned per stage, and HARNESS_CONFIG.md versions the runtime permission/hook rules. Each rolls back independently: a prompt regression does not imply the model or config caused it, and rolling back one axis while the others stay pinned is how MODEL_LIFECYCLE.md's per-stage rollback trigger stays meaningful.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a PERSONAS.md for an AI workflow. Distinguish two persona classes: (1) Recipient — who consumes the workflow output to make decisions, and (2) Operator — who maintains/tunes/monitors the workflow. agent_hints.instruction: Generate a CONSTRAINTS.md documenting all fixed constraints the AI workflow must operate within. Cover: privacy/compliance (PDPA, data residency, what data the LLM may/may not see), model availability (which Claude/GPT models are accessible, regional availability), cost ceiling (per-run, monthly), latency/schedule (must complete by X time, max processing duration), and integration constraints (which MCP servers, API rate limits, OAuth scope).
agent_hints.input_context: Gather from stakeholder interviews, vendor SLAs, and corporate IT policy. These are non-negotiable inputs to harness design.
agent_hints.validation: Must address all five constraint categories. Each constraint must be stated as a clear, testable requirement (e.g., 'cost per run must not exceed ฿20'). Any budget, rate limit or retention period not yet calibrated must be declared null with its calibration owner rather than filled with a placeholder number that later reads as agreed.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a VPD.md using the Value Proposition Canvas adapted for AI workflows. Customer = Recipient persona. Jobs = decisions/tasks the recipient does that the workflow assists. Pain = friction in current workflow (cognitive load, time spent, things missed). Gain = time saved, clarity gained, decisions made better. Pain Relievers and Gain Creators are produced by the workflow output (the brief/report/action). e.g., Pain: 'recipient spends 45 min/day scanning inbox', Gain: 'zero missed urgent items', Pain Reliever: 'auto-classify + prioritize → brief delivered by 07:30'.

agent_hints.validation: Must contain at least one entry for each of: customer_jobs, pains, gains, pain_relievers, gain_creators, value_propositions. Each pain reliever must link back to a pain; each gain creator must link to a gain.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a WRD.md (Workflow Requirements Document). Write a clear problem statement, define measurable success metrics (precision/recall on action detection, recipient satisfaction, time saved per day), list workflow stories in 'When [trigger], the workflow [does action], so that [recipient gets value]' format, categorize functional requirements as P0/P1/P2 (each requirement names which trigger/transform/output it concerns), specify NFRs (latency, cost per run, accuracy thresholds), and define output acceptance criteria per output section.
agent_hints.input_context: Reference personas, vpd, scope, and constraints. Every workflow story must map to a recipient persona and at least one decision in PERSONAS.md.
agent_hints.validation: Every functional requirement must have a priority and an acceptance criterion. Every workflow story must reference a persona ID. Every NFR must have a measurable threshold. Every functional requirement must carry a stable Requirement ID that downstream documents can reference.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a GLOSSARY.md defining the workflow's ubiquitous language. Collect every business term used by personas and in WRD.md workflow stories — especially terms where different roles disagree (e.g., 'urgent' to an operator vs 'urgent' to a recipient). Give each term one agreed definition, its owner role, and synonyms that must NOT appear in schema fields or prompt variables. Map every term to where it is implemented: a classification taxonomy label in DATA_CONTRACTS.md, a schema field, or a prompt variable in PROMPT_SPEC.md. Record disputed terms with the competing definitions and the resolution. LLM classification quality depends on these definitions being unambiguous — they become the ground truth for the golden dataset labels.
agent_hints.input_context: Terms originate from PERSONAS.md profiles and WRD.md workflow stories. Every classification label used downstream in DATA_CONTRACTS.md must trace back to a term defined here. The Enumeration Registry section is the single index of every enum used across the project, and it has two kinds of row. These exist in every project built from this template: requirement_priority (WRD.md), work_item_status (TASKS.md), classification_taxonomy_value and data_classification (DATA_CONTRACTS.md), prompt_id (PROMPT_SPEC.md), stage_id and agent_role (HARNESS.md), adr_status (ADR.md), error_code and failure_class (INTEGRATION_SPEC.md), side_effect_class (HARNESS_CONFIG.md), eval_metric_name (EVALUATION.md), deployment_status (MODEL_LIFECYCLE.md) and incident_severity (RUNBOOK.md). On top of those, register every domain enum this project's own documents own — the template cannot name them in advance because they come from the workflow being automated, so the registry is always longer than this list and its length differs per project. Note that requirement_priority and incident_severity share the symbols P0/P1/P2 while being different scales with different owners; the registry keeps them apart by name. This document indexes; it never redefines a value owned elsewhere.
agent_hints.validation: Every term must have exactly one definition and one owner role. Every classification taxonomy label must map to a term. Disputed terms must record the resolution. No orphan terms that map to nothing. The Enumeration Registry must map every enum listed in input_context, plus every domain enum any document in this set owns, to exactly one owner document and contain zero enum values. Walk it in both directions — from each registry row to the owner document that declares the values, and from every enum the documents actually use back to a registry row.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a HARNESS.md. Begin with a Mermaid diagram showing the end-to-end pipeline. Document each stage (trigger, collector, filter, classifier, extractor, synthesizer, evaluator, delivery, memory) with its responsibility, inputs, outputs, and success criteria. Define the agent roles using GAN-inspired pattern (Planner / Generator / Evaluator) and explain why each is a separate agent. State which Claude model is used at each stage and why (Haiku for cheap classification, Opus for synthesis). Document control flow including retries, branches, and circuit breakers. Critically, list failure modes with their mitigation — every harness component must encode an explicit assumption about what the model can't do alone.
agent_hints.input_context: Must satisfy WRD.md functional/non-functional requirements within CONSTRAINTS.md. Each stage maps to one or more functional requirements.
agent_hints.validation: Every stage must have: id, responsibility, inputs[], outputs[], model_used (or 'none'), failure_modes[]. Mermaid diagram must be valid syntax. Every failure mode must have at least one mitigation. Every retry count, backoff window and circuit-breaker threshold must be either a calibrated value with its source or null with a named calibration owner — never a guessed default.

optional_integrations.description: The Cost and Latency Profile section's per-stage budgets, thresholds and retry/backoff parameters — declared null with a named calibration owner until measured — may optionally take calibration evidence, candidate values, or a measurement methodology from an optimization-theory run's deployment governance record. HARNESS.md remains the sole owner of the configured value; a null is replaced only when backed by a stated, project-accepted measurement recorded here, never by copying the external record's number directly. Optional: the null-plus-owner discipline this document requires works without it.

This harness may optionally execute another track's scheduled operational job — for example ai-chatbot's Knowledge Base ingestion/refresh job — as one of its pipeline stages, instead of that track running an ad hoc script. HARNESS.md remains the sole owner of its own pipeline/stage/control-flow contract; the consuming track's operations document remains the sole owner of what the job must accomplish and its acceptance criteria. Optional: this document's own pipeline is complete without ever being consumed this way.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a SECURITY_PRIVACY.md focused on AI-workflow-specific concerns. description.en: Audit log requirements for every LLM call and stage.

items.text_th: GIST — log ที่ไม่มี identifier ร่วมเชื่อม per-call กับ per-stage เข้าด้วยกัน คือกองข้อมูลที่ตอบไม่ได้ว่า output ที่ส่งไปหาผู้รับเมื่อวานมาจาก input ชุดไหน — audit log มีค่าตอนที่ join ได้ ไม่ใช่ตอนที่เก็บครบ
items.text_en: GIST — logs with no shared identifier joining the per-call and per-stage records cannot answer which inputs produced the output delivered yesterday; an audit log earns its keep by being joinable, not by being complete

items.text_th: Per-call Log — model, prompt hash, token count, cost, latency, timestamp
items.text_en: Per-call Log — model, prompt hash, token count, cost, latency, timestamp

items.text_th: Per-stage Log — stage id, status, duration, output schema validation result
items.text_en: Per-stage Log — stage id, status, duration, output schema validation result

items.text_th: Retention Period — เก็บ log นานแค่ไหน
items.text_en: Retention Period — log retention duration

items.text_th: Run Identity — ทุก record ทั้ง per-call และ per-stage ต้องมี run_id เดียวกันของ run นั้น พร้อม parent/child id เมื่อ subagent ถูกเรียก — นี่คือสิ่งเดียวที่ทำให้ log สองระดับ join กันได้
items.text_en: Run Identity — every record, per-call and per-stage alike, carries the same run_id for that execution plus parent/child ids when a subagent is invoked; this is the only thing that makes the two log levels joinable

items.text_th: Immutability — log record ไม่ถูกแก้ย้อนหลัง การแก้คือการเขียน record ใหม่ที่อ้าง record เดิม — log ที่แก้ทับได้ใช้เป็นหลักฐาน audit ไม่ได้
items.text_en: Immutability — a log record is never edited in place; a correction is a new record citing the old one — a log that can be overwritten is not audit evidence

items.text_th: Required Audit Queries — คำถามที่ log ต้องตอบได้จริง: output ที่ส่งเมื่อวานมาจาก input และ prompt version ไหน, run ไหนบ้างที่ใช้ model version ที่เพิ่ง rollback, tool call ไหนที่ PERMISSION_DENIED ในสัปดาห์นี้
items.text_en: Required Audit Queries — the questions the log must actually answer: which inputs and prompt version produced yesterday's delivered output, which runs used the model version just rolled back, and which tool calls returned PERMISSION_DENIED this week

agent_hints.instruction: Generate an INTEGRATION_SPEC.md. Document every integration the workflow makes. For triggers (inbound): the platform (cron in Make.com, webhook), schedule/event, payload schema. For MCP tool calls: the MCP server, the specific tool name (e.g., ZohoMailRead.searchEmails), the call parameters, the expected response schema. For delivery channels (outbound): the destination (Craft daily note, ZohoCliq DM), the format payload, success criteria. Document error codes per integration, retry policy, rate-limit handling, and versioning.
agent_hints.input_context: Every integration referenced in HARNESS.md must be documented here. Schemas must align with DATA_CONTRACTS.md.
agent_hints.validation: Every MCP tool call must have: server, tool_name, parameters, response_schema, error_codes[]. Every delivery channel must have: destination, format, success_criteria, retry_policy. Every retry count, backoff window and timeout must be a calibrated value with its source or null with a named calibration owner. Every error code must carry a cause class and be classified retryable or terminal; partial completion is recorded as a separate flag, never as a cause class.

items.text_th: Delivery Guarantee — ระบุว่าช่องทางนี้เป็น at-most-once หรือ at-least-once และผลที่ตามมา — at-least-once แปลว่าผู้รับอาจเห็นซ้ำ จึงต้องมี dedup key
items.text_en: Delivery Guarantee — state whether this channel is at-most-once or at-least-once and what follows from it — at-least-once means the recipient may see duplicates, so a dedup key is required

items.text_th: Dedup Key — คีย์ที่ผู้รับหรือ adapter ใช้ตัดข้อความซ้ำเมื่อ retry (เช่น run_id + destination) — retry ที่ไม่มี dedup key คือการส่งซ้ำให้ผู้รับจริง
items.text_en: Dedup Key — the key the recipient or adapter uses to discard a duplicate on retry (e.g. run_id + destination); a retry without a dedup key delivers the message twice to a real person

items.text_th: Ordering Guarantee — ระบุว่าลำดับสำคัญหรือไม่ และรักษาอย่างไรเมื่อส่งหลายชิ้นจาก run เดียว หรือประกาศตรง ๆ ว่าไม่รับประกันลำดับ
items.text_en: Ordering Guarantee — state whether order matters and how it is preserved when one run delivers several pieces, or declare explicitly that no ordering is guaranteed

description.th: Error codes ของแต่ละ integration และ policy การ retry
description.en: Per-integration error codes and retry policies.

items.text_th: Retryable ≠ Terminal — error ที่ retry ได้คือ error ชั่วคราวที่การลองใหม่มีโอกาสสำเร็จ (timeout, 429, upstream 5xx); error ที่ terminal คือ retry แล้วก็ได้ผลเดิม (invalid input, permission denied, precondition failed) — retry error ประเภทหลังคือการเผา budget และ rate limit ไปเปล่า ๆ
items.text_en: Retryable ≠ Terminal — a retryable error is transient and a repeat attempt may succeed (timeout, 429, upstream 5xx); a terminal error returns the same result no matter how often it is retried (invalid input, permission denied, precondition failed) — retrying the latter class only burns budget and rate limit

items.text_th: Error Code — เช่น ZOHO_AUTH_FAILED, MCP_TIMEOUT
items.text_en: Error Code — e.g. ZOHO_AUTH_FAILED, MCP_TIMEOUT

items.text_th: Retry Strategy — กี่ครั้ง, backoff, jitter
items.text_en: Retry Strategy — count, backoff, jitter

items.text_th: Escalation — แจ้ง operator เมื่อใด
items.text_en: Escalation — when to alert the operator

items.text_th: Failure Class — ทุก error code จัดเข้าหนึ่ง cause class: INVALID_INPUT, PERMISSION_DENIED, PRECONDITION_FAILED, UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT หรือ RATE_LIMITED — enum นี้เป็นเจ้าของโดยเอกสารนี้ และกำหนดว่า retryable หรือ terminal ส่วนความสำเร็จบางส่วนเป็น outcome flag แยกต่างหาก ไม่ใช่ cause class ดู PARTIAL_RESULT Handling ด้านล่าง
items.text_en: Failure Class — every error code maps to exactly one cause class: INVALID_INPUT, PERMISSION_DENIED, PRECONDITION_FAILED, UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT or RATE_LIMITED; this enum is owned here and decides retryable vs terminal. Partial completion is a separate outcome flag, not a cause class — see PARTIAL_RESULT Handling below

items.text_th: Partial Completion — tool ที่สำเร็จบางส่วน (ส่งได้ 3 จาก 5 ปลายทาง) ตั้ง partial-result flag คู่กับ cause class ของส่วนที่ล้ม และระบุว่าถือเป็นสำเร็จ ล้มเหลว หรือ retry เฉพาะส่วนที่เหลือ — retry ต้องไม่ทำซ้ำส่วนที่สำเร็จแล้ว
items.text_en: Partial Completion — a tool that partially succeeded (3 of 5 destinations delivered) sets a partial-result flag alongside the cause class of the part that failed, and declares whether that counts as success, failure, or a retry of only the remainder — the retry must never repeat what already succeeded

items.text_th: Idempotency Key per Call — tool call ที่มี side effect ต้องส่ง idempotency key เพื่อให้ retry ปลอดภัย ถ้า provider ไม่รองรับ ต้องระบุกลไกกันซ้ำฝั่งเราแทน
items.text_en: Idempotency Key per Call — every side-effecting tool call carries an idempotency key so a retry is safe; when the provider offers none, state the dedup mechanism used on our side instead

items.text_th: Drift Response — เมื่อจับ drift ได้: หยุด stage นั้น, route เข้า quarantine ตาม RUNBOOK.md, แจ้งเจ้าของ integration — ห้ามปล่อยให้ payload รูปแบบใหม่ไหลต่อเข้า LLM
items.text_en: Drift Response — on detection: halt that stage, route the run to quarantine per RUNBOOK.md, and notify the integration owner — never let an unrecognized payload shape flow onward into the LLM

description.th: ชั้น enforcement ของ harness — permission rules, tool allowlist, hooks, sandbox, MCP server registration ที่บังคับด้วย configuration ไม่ใช่ prompt
description.en: The enforcement layer of the harness — permission rules, tool allowlists, hooks, sandbox, and MCP server registration enforced by configuration rather than prompts.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a HARNESS_CONFIG.md documenting the enforcement layer of the harness — everything that constrains agent behavior via configuration rather than prompt text. Document the permission mode per environment, allow/deny rules per tool pattern, and the tool allowlist per agent role from HARNESS.md. List every lifecycle hook (event, script, rule it enforces) and state explicitly which rules are enforced by hooks versus merely requested in prompts. Specify the execution environment and sandbox boundaries plus resource limits (timeout, max turns, token budget per run). Document every registered MCP server with its scopes, credential binding, and which stages may call its tools. Describe the configuration file layout and what is version-controlled versus local-only.
agent_hints.input_context: Enforcement counterpart of the HARNESS.md design. Must cover every agent role in HARNESS.md and every MCP server in INTEGRATION_SPEC.md. Secret storage follows SECURITY_PRIVACY.md.
agent_hints.validation: Every agent role in HARNESS.md must have a tool allowlist entry. Every MCP server in INTEGRATION_SPEC.md must appear in the server registry with explicit scopes. Every hook must name the rule it enforces. Rules that must hold in production cannot rely on prompt text alone — each must map to a permission rule or hook. Every resource limit (timeout, max turns, token budget) must be a calibrated value with its source or null with a named calibration owner.

description.th: Permission mode และ allow/deny rules ที่คุมว่า agent ทำอะไรได้โดยไม่ต้องขอ
description.en: Permission modes and allow/deny rules controlling what agents may do without approval.

items.text_th: GIST — permission model คือชั้นที่บังคับได้จริง ต่างจาก prompt ที่ 'ขอความร่วมมือ' — กฎที่ต้องเป็นจริงใน production ห้ามพึ่ง prompt text อย่างเดียว ต้อง map ไปเป็น permission rule หรือ hook เสมอ
items.text_en: GIST — the permission model is the layer that actually enforces, unlike a prompt which merely requests; any rule that must hold in production cannot rest on prompt text alone and must map to a permission rule or a hook

items.text_th: Permission Mode per Environment — dev/staging/production ใช้ mode ใด (interactive approval, auto-accept, bypass)
items.text_en: Permission Mode per Environment — which mode each of dev/staging/production uses (interactive approval, auto-accept, bypass)

items.text_th: Allow/Deny Rules — rule ต่อ tool pattern (เช่น allow read-only, deny destructive commands)
items.text_en: Allow/Deny Rules — rules per tool pattern (e.g. allow read-only, deny destructive commands)

items.text_th: Approval Escalation — action ใดต้องหยุดรอ human approval เสมอ สอดคล้อง HITL checkpoints
items.text_en: Approval Escalation — actions that must always pause for human approval, aligned with HITL checkpoints

description.en: Which tools each agent role may use, following least privilege.

items.text_en: Per-Role Allowlist — map each agent role in HARNESS.md to its permitted tools

items.text_th: Least Privilege Rationale — เหตุผลที่แต่ละ role ได้สิทธิ์เท่าที่จำเป็น
items.text_en: Least Privilege Rationale — why each role gets only the access it needs

items.text_th: Denied-by-Default List — tools ที่ปิดทุก role เว้นแต่ระบุชัด
items.text_en: Denied-by-Default List — tools disabled for every role unless explicitly granted

items.text_th: Side-Effect Class — ทุก tool ประกาศว่าการเขียนไปลงที่ไหน: READ_ONLY, WRITE_INTERNAL หรือ WRITE_EXTERNAL (enum นี้เป็นเจ้าของโดยเอกสารนี้) และมี irreversible flag แยกต่างหากสำหรับผลที่ย้อนกลับไม่ได้ — tool หนึ่งเป็นได้ทั้ง WRITE_EXTERNAL และ irreversible โดย irreversible flag เป็นตัวกำหนดระดับ approval เสมอ
items.text_en: Side-Effect Class — every tool declares where its write lands: READ_ONLY, WRITE_INTERNAL or WRITE_EXTERNAL (this enum is owned here), plus a separate irreversible flag for effects that cannot be undone. A tool may be both WRITE_EXTERNAL and irreversible; the irreversible flag always sets the approval requirement

items.text_th: Irreversible Requires Approval — tool ที่ติด irreversible flag (ส่งอีเมลออกนอกองค์กร, ลบข้อมูล, จ่ายเงิน) ต้องผูกกับ HITL checkpoint ใน HARNESS.md เสมอ และห้ามให้ agent เรียกเองอัตโนมัติใน production
items.text_en: Irreversible Requires Approval — any tool flagged irreversible (sending external email, deleting data, moving money) must be bound to a HITL checkpoint in HARNESS.md and never auto-invoked by an agent in production

items.text_en: Injection Guard Hooks — hooks that inspect/block dangerous input per the SECURITY_PRIVACY.md threat model

items.text_en: Resource Limits — timeout, max turns, token budget per run

items.text_th: Config File Inventory — ไฟล์ config ทั้งหมด (settings, permission rules, hook scripts) และตำแหน่ง
items.text_en: Config File Inventory — every config file (settings, permission rules, hook scripts) and its location

items.text_en: Version Control Policy — which configs are committed versus local-only/secret

description.th: แผนการจัดวาง context ของ harness — ความรู้ชั้นไหนโหลดเมื่อไหร่ (always-loaded, on-trigger skills, cross-session memory), context budget ต่อ stage, และการแยก context ด้วย subagent
description.en: Context layout plan for the harness — which knowledge loads when (always-loaded, on-trigger skills, cross-session memory), context budget per stage, and context isolation via subagents.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a CONTEXT_PLAN.md defining where every piece of knowledge in the workflow lives and when it enters the model's context. Define the context layers (always-loaded instruction files, on-trigger skills, cross-session memory, per-run input) and placement rules for each kind of knowledge. Inventory every skill with the trigger description that loads it. Document the memory strategy: what persists across runs, its schema per DATA_CONTRACTS.md, and write/expiry policy. agent_hints.instruction: Generate an EVALUATION.md. Define the eval strategy: when to run (per-prompt change, per-release, continuous on production samples), what to measure (precision, recall, F1 for classifications; citation grounding for synthesis; hallucination rate; schema compliance; latency; cost). Document the golden dataset — curated input/output pairs used for offline eval. Specify each eval metric with threshold (e.g., 'citation grounding ≥ 99%', 'hallucination rate ≤ 1%'). Document the citation grounding test (every claim must trace back to a real input). Document the hallucination detection method (separate evaluator agent, programmatic schema check). Document the format compliance test (output validates against DATA_CONTRACTS.md schemas). Define the recipient feedback loop — how user feedback (thumbs up/down, written comment) feeds back into eval set.
agent_hints.input_context: Eval cases must cover all output acceptance criteria in WRD.md. Eval thresholds from CONSTRAINTS.md. Read references/noisy-evaluation-and-budget.md for why an LLM-judge is a noisy evaluator (Ū = U + ε), and why repeated evaluation and a minimum meaningful difference are required before calling a change a regression. Read references/contract-dsl-to-runtime-validation.md §6 for the one-failing/one-passing-fixture-per-criterion pattern when building the golden dataset.
agent_hints.validation: Every output acceptance criterion in WRD.md must have at least one eval case. Every eval metric must have either a numeric threshold with its calibration source or null with a named calibration owner — never an uncalibrated number presented as settled. Golden dataset size must be stated with the coverage rule that justifies it (at minimum one case per classification class plus edge cases). The eval strategy must distinguish offline (pre-deploy, fixed dataset) from online (post-deploy, production sample) and define both.

optional_integrations.description: This document's eval metrics may optionally enter an optimization-theory run as evaluators — functions the optimization process scores candidates against — never as objectives the optimization process is free to trade off by default. EVALUATION.md remains the sole owner of each metric's definition, threshold and calibration source; optimization-theory only consumes them as-is to judge candidates. Optional: this document's own eval strategy is complete without optimization-theory.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a MODEL_LIFECYCLE.md governing how models are pinned, upgraded, and rolled back. Providers deprecate models on their own schedule — this document is the playbook for surviving that churn. Inventory every model used per stage from HARNESS.md with its exact pinned ID (never an alias like 'latest'). Define the response to a provider deprecation notice: timeline, owner, candidate selection. Every model swap must pass the re-evaluation gate: re-run the full golden dataset from EVALUATION.md, compare eval metrics against the current model, and block the upgrade if any metric regresses beyond the stated threshold. Prompts may need re-calibration per PROMPT_SPEC.md when the model changes — treat a model swap as a prompt version bump. Define rollback: how fast, triggered by what eval or production signal, and who decides.
agent_hints.input_context: Model-per-stage assignments come from HARNESS.md. The golden dataset and eval metrics come from EVALUATION.md. Prompt re-calibration procedures come from PROMPT_SPEC.md versioning rules. Read references/noisy-evaluation-and-budget.md before setting the re-evaluation gate — a single run that moves a metric is not evidence of regression; the gate needs repeated evaluation and a stated minimum meaningful difference, not just a raw threshold.
agent_hints.validation: Every stage's model must have an exact pinned ID. The re-evaluation gate must state a regression threshold per eval metric. Rollback must specify trigger signals and maximum time-to-rollback. Deprecation playbook must have an owner and timeline. Each regression threshold must state the minimum meaningful difference it is based on, or be null with a named calibration owner — a single run that moves a metric is not evidence of regression.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a README.md. Include a one-paragraph description of what the workflow does, the cadence, and the recipient. Provide a quick-start aimed at operators (not end users) — how to verify the workflow is alive, where to see logs, how to flag a problem. List prerequisites (Make.com seat, MCP credentials, Anthropic API key). Provide activation steps for a fresh deployment. Describe daily usage (what the recipient sees, where to give feedback). Brief architecture overview with link to HARNESS.md. Contributing guidelines (how to propose a prompt change, how to add a new stage). License.
agent_hints.input_context: Use SCOPE.md for workflow description, HARNESS.md for architecture overview, DEPLOYMENT_OPS.md for activation steps.
agent_hints.validation: Must include a working quick-start that an operator can follow on day one to verify the workflow is healthy. Must link to all canonical documents (HARNESS.md, PROMPT_SPEC.md, RUNBOOK.md). Activation steps must be testable without access to production data.
